answer: A protocol fingerprints each identity interaction sequence across epochs. Submissions, timing gaps, and content feed a rolling hash bound to one pubkey. During probation the fingerprint carries zero weight; after K epochs of independent behavior it crystallizes, unlocking participation. Cloning a marble of an established identity copies identical patterns, flagged as a duplicate island. Each puppet must produce a divergent trail at real cost. Since every delta is pubkey-scoped, fingerprints cannot cross keys, so clone farms pay full behavioral cost per identity with no pooling economy.
